MFN pricing granted by Vendor to us remains welcome."}},{"ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0045"],"quote":"Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"This is a 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — our walk-away position, and it also contradicts Section 12.3.","confidence":0.93,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0045","oldText":"12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","newText":"12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other Party who was directly involved in providing or receiving the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by an individual.","comment":"[Playbook] We have narrowed this to our fallback: a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with the usual general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. We cannot accept a no-hire provision."}},{"ruleId":"T4C","status":"missing","paragraphIds":["p0036","p0039","p0032"],"quote":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.","rationale":"Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and Vendor-default termination. There is no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a three-year term, which is a deviation from our position.","confidence":0.88,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0039","oldText":"A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","newText":"A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

9.6 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination.","comment":"[Playbook] We have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund; the three-year term otherwise locks us in with no exit. Our fallback is 60–90 days' notice."}},{"ruleId":"RENEWAL","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0033","p0034"],"quote":"renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal","rationale":"12-month renewals, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day Vendor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% match our preferred position.","confidence":0.92},{"ruleId":"GOVLAW","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0103","p0104"],"quote":"This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","rationale":"Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue fall outside our accepted list and contradict Section 28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts.","confidence":0.95,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0103","oldText":"This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","newText":"This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.","comment":"[Playbook] We have moved governing law to New York, our preferred position, which also resolves the conflict with Section 28.2's exclusive New York venue. Delaware, California or England and Wales would be acceptable fallbacks."}},{"ruleId":"ASSIGN","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0087","p0088","p0090"],"quote":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.","rationale":"Customer has an affiliate/successor assignment right without consent, Vendor assignment requires our consent and is barred to competitors, and no Vendor right arises on our change of control.","confidence":0.93},{"ruleId":"IP","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0054","p0055"],"quote":"Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","newText":"14.2 Customer exclusively owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to each such Deliverable upon creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and Customer receives the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence set out in Section 13.2 for any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable.","comment":"[Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have reversed the assignment and preserved Vendor's ownership of its pre-existing technology with the licence-back in Section 13.2. Our minimum fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables."}},{"ruleId":"LICENSE","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0048","p0049","p0050"],"quote":"Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services","rationale":"The grant covers Affiliates and contractors, paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, transfer to a successor is permitted, and suspension is limited to uncured material breach.","confidence":0.9},{"ruleId":"AUDIT","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0082","p0083"],"quote":"Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice","rationale":"Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access — matches our preferred position.","confidence":0.93},{"ruleId":"LD","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0028","p0101"],"quote":"Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","rationale":"","confidence":0.7},{"ruleId":"WARRANTY","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0071","p0072","p0074","p0075"],"quote":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.","rationale":"Professional-services warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance (Services for the whole term), compliance with law, no malicious code, and a repair/replace/refund remedy; the disclaimer expressly preserves the express warranties.","confidence":0.91},{"ruleId":"INSURANCE","status":"compliant","paragraphIds":["p0068","p0069"],"quote":"commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000","rationale":"Coverage limits, the one-year tail and certificates on request meet our preferred position.","confidence":0.95},{"ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","status":"deviation","paragraphIds":["p0012","p0044"],"quote":"Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"A three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is our walk-away position, and it contradicts Section 12.3's statement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.","confidence":0.94,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0012","oldText":"2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","newText":"2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services during the current twelve-month term. Multi-year take-or-pay with no exit is not something we can accept, and it conflicts with Section 12.3."}},{"ruleId":"TRANSITION","status":"missing","paragraphIds":["p0041","p0042"],"quote":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period.","rationale":"Section 10 addresses access, Deliverables and refunds but contains no obligation to provide transition assistance, return Customer Data in a machine-readable format, or certify deletion (and the cross-referenced Section 11 is absent).","confidence":0.86,"replacement":{"paragraphId":"p0042","oldText":"Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","newText":"Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of request, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements.","comment":"[Playbook] We have added exit protections: transition assistance for up to six months, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion. Our fallback is 90 days of assistance with the same export timing."}}]}

findings.quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000.
findings.rationale: Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees (paid or payable) and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and the full carve-out set, with Customer's payment obligations excluded from the cap. Matches our preferred position.

findings.quote: infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5
findings.rationale: There is no indemnification section in the Agreement — Section 20 is missing entirely even though Section 9.3 cross-references "Section 20.5" and Section 21.3 treats "indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims. We need a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity.

replacement.oldText: Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.
replacement.newText:
Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

21.5 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give prompt notice of the claim, Vendor shall control the defence, and Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have added the Vendor indemnity: the Agreement omits Section 20 altogether, yet Sections 9.3 and 21.3 both cross-reference indemnification. Our position is a Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, sitting outside the liability cap.

findings.quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
findings.rationale: An undefined, worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer is at our walk-away threshold and directly contradicts Section 12.3, which confirms Customer has made no non-compete commitment.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this clause: we cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, and it contradicts Section 12.3. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could discuss a named-product restriction limited to the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

findings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
findings.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer; Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage any supplier.

findings.quote: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
findings.rationale: This is an MFN/right-to-match obligation running against us — an open-ended duty to disclose and match third-party offers. Our position is that MFNs may only run in Customer's favour.

replacement.oldText: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this provision: we cannot commit to disclose or match third-party offers, and it conflicts with Section 12.3. MFN pricing granted by Vendor to us remains welcome.

findings.quote: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
findings.rationale: This is a 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — our walk-away position, and it also contradicts Section 12.3.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
replacement.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other Party who was directly involved in providing or receiving the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by an individual.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed this to our fallback: a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with the usual general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. We cannot accept a no-hire provision.

findings.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.
findings.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and Vendor-default termination. There is no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a three-year term, which is a deviation from our position.

replacement.oldText: A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
replacement.newText:
A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

9.6 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund; the three-year term otherwise locks us in with no exit. Our fallback is 60–90 days' notice.

findings.quote: renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal
findings.rationale: 12-month renewals, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day Vendor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% match our preferred position.

findings.quote: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.rationale: Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue fall outside our accepted list and contradict Section 28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts.

replacement.oldText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
replacement.newText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law to New York, our preferred position, which also resolves the conflict with Section 28.2's exclusive New York venue. Delaware, California or England and Wales would be acceptable fallbacks.

findings.quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
findings.rationale: Customer has an affiliate/successor assignment right without consent, Vendor assignment requires our consent and is barred to competitors, and no Vendor right arises on our change of control.

findings.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
findings.rationale: We do not accept Vendor ownership of Deliverables we pay for coupled with a revocable, term-limited, non-transferable licence. This also conflicts with the perpetual licence in Sections 13.2, 13.3 and the transfer right in 13.3.

replacement.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
replacement.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to each such Deliverable upon creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and Customer receives the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence set out in Section 13.2 for any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have reversed the assignment and preserved Vendor's ownership of its pre-existing technology with the licence-back in Section 13.2. Our minimum fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables.

findings.quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services
findings.rationale: The grant covers Affiliates and contractors, paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, transfer to a successor is permitted, and suspension is limited to uncured material breach.

findings.quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice
findings.rationale: Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access — matches our preferred position.

findings.quote: Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
findings.rationale: Professional-services warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance (Services for the whole term), compliance with law, no malicious code, and a repair/replace/refund remedy; the disclaimer expressly preserves the express warranties.

findings.quote: commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
findings.rationale: Coverage limits, the one-year tail and certificates on request meet our preferred position.

findings.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
findings.rationale: A three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is our walk-away position, and it contradicts Section 12.3's statement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

replacement.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
replacement.newText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services during the current twelve-month term. Customer may reduce that commitment on thirty days' written notice, and any shortfall will be addressed by a true-up of Fees rather than a penalty. Customer has no purchase commitment for any subsequent period unless agreed in a signed Order Form.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed this to our fallback: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of take-or-pay. Multi-year take-or-pay with no exit is not something we can accept, and it conflicts with Section 12.3.

findings.quote: On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period.
findings.rationale: Section 10 addresses access, Deliverables and refunds but contains no obligation to provide transition assistance, return Customer Data in a machine-readable format, or certify deletion (and the cross-referenced Section 11 is absent).

replacement.oldText: Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
replacement.newText:
Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of request, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have added exit protections: transition assistance for up to six months, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion. Our fallback is 90 days of assistance with the same export timing.
